exposure: Birth in a first level peripheral hospital
cohort: 816 women who gave birth at a first level peripheral hospital in Cefalù, Italy, between January 2017 and December 2018
finding: Despite a low volume of births, the peripheral hospital demonstrated low rates of maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity, suggesting that adequate perinatal care can be provided in such settings.
mod_finding: 434 vaginal deliveries (53%) and 382 caesarean sections (47%) were performed.
gest_age: Majority of pregnancies were at term (96%)
